findings: The fixed-checkpoint, no-update comparison is a focused test of whether this model’s predictions and recurrent states depend on carried GRU state beyond 256 rows when the canonical 211-wide causal inputs are held identical. The design keeps causal feature history intact, so it does not confound recurrent-state truncation with feature-history reset.

The FULL branch is correctly specified as one continuous stream across both anchors, with independent branch states for RECENT256 and ZERO. The declared forward-row accounting is consistent: 130,048 non-rollout full-prefix rows plus 10,240 branch/rollout rows equals 140,288 total rows for eight sequences.

The fixed R3 fit-only component selection, no-target-use rule, no evaluation arrays, no score/backward/update, source/checkpoint identities, strict loader, fixed positions/windows, state and model invariants, compact sufficient statistics, and fail-closed CPU/resource limits are concrete and suitable for this bounded diagnostic.
implementation_acceptance_note: Keep k=0 defined as the state immediately before consuming the anchor row, process the same [anchor, anchor+128) feature rows for all three branches, and clone FULL state for window observations so recording a rollout cannot alter the continuous stream into the next anchor.
limits_preserved: Output differences measure dependence on recurrent carry for one stored checkpoint and fixed inputs; they do not show that the erased history is predictively useful or that longer raw history is unnecessary.
The same canonical causal features already contain their own history, so this does not test total history dependence or reset the input-feature state.
The eight sequences and sixteen windows are an exposed-panel diagnostic, not independent replications or a population/evaluation estimate.
The 1% relative and 1e-3 absolute scales are descriptive references only; the test produces no quality grade or campaign acceptance decision.
review_scope: Read-only pre-code design critique; no checkpoint, arrays, model outputs, remote actions, or new fitting.
